The coma can expand to hundreds of thousands of kilometers.

## **14. Comets**

Comets are small Solar System bodies containing substantial amounts of volatile ices, dust, and rock.

When a comet approaches the Sun, solar heating causes some of its volatile material to transition directly from solid to gas.

This process creates a surrounding coma.

Solar radiation and the solar wind can push material away from the comet, producing tails.

The dust tail and ion tail can point in directions influenced by different physical processes.

Comets are scientifically important because they can preserve primitive material from the early Solar System.

Long-period comets may originate from the distant Oort Cloud.

Short-period comets are often associated with the Kuiper Belt and related populations.

Saturn rotates very rapidly.
A Saturnian day lasts approximately 10.7 hours.
Rapid rotation causes Saturn to have a large equatorial bulge.

The energy produced in the core travels outward through several layers. In the radiative zone, energy is transferred primarily through radiation. In the convective zone, hot plasma rises while cooler material sinks, producing convection.

## STAR FORMATION

Stars form inside cold, dense regions of interstellar clouds.
These regions contain gas and microscopic dust grains.
Gravity causes sufficiently dense parts of a cloud to collapse.
As a collapsing region contracts, its density and temperature increase.
The collapsing material can form a protostar.
A protostar is a young stellar object that has not yet begun stable hydrogen fusion.
Material can continue falling onto the protostar from its surrounding disk.
Conservation of angular momentum causes the material to rotate faster as it contracts.
A circumstellar disk can form around the young star.
Planets can eventually form from material remaining in such disks.

## 7. CORONA

The corona is the outermost major layer of the solar atmosphere.
The corona extends millions of kilometers from the visible solar surface.
The corona is extremely hot compared with the photosphere.
Coronal temperatures can reach millions of degrees Celsius.
The low density of the corona allows it to extend far into space.
The corona is visible during a total solar eclipse.
Special instruments called coronagraphs can observe the corona by blocking direct sunlight.
The corona contains plasma influenced by the Sun's magnetic field.
Coronal holes are regions where magnetic field structures allow enhanced solar wind escape.
The solar wind originates in the Sun's outer atmosphere.

COMA
The coma is a cloud of gas and dust surrounding an active nucleus.
It forms when solar heating causes volatile materials to escape.
The coma can expand to hundreds of thousands of kilometers.
Its size depends on the comet's activity and distance from the Sun.
The coma contains molecules released directly from the nucleus.
Solar radiation can break these molecules into smaller fragments.

## **14. Comets**

Comets are small Solar System bodies containing substantial amounts of volatile ices, dust, and rock.

When a comet approaches the Sun, solar heating causes some of its volatile material to transition directly from solid to gas.

This process creates a surrounding coma.

Solar radiation and the solar wind can push material away from the comet, producing tails.

The dust tail and ion tail can point in directions influenced by different physical processes.

Comets are scientifically important because they can preserve primitive material from the early Solar System.

Long-period comets may originate from the distant Oort Cloud.

Short-period comets are often associated with the Kuiper Belt and related populations.

## 5. ROTATION

Saturn rotates very rapidly.
A Saturnian day lasts approximately 10.7 hours.
Rapid rotation causes Saturn to have a large equatorial bulge.

## STAR FORMATION

Stars form inside cold, dense regions of interstellar clouds.
These regions contain gas and microscopic dust grains.
Gravity causes sufficiently dense parts of a cloud to collapse.
As a collapsing region contracts, its density and temperature increase.
The collapsing material can form a protostar.
A protostar is a young stellar object that has not yet begun stable hydrogen fusion.
Material can continue falling onto the protostar from its surrounding disk.
Conservation of angular momentum causes the material to rotate faster as it contracts.
A circumstellar disk can form around the young star.
Planets can eventually form from material remaining in such disks.

## 5. ROTATION

Jupiter rotates extremely rapidly.
One rotation takes approximately 9 hours and 56 minutes.
Jupiter has the shortest rotation period of all eight planets.
Rapid rotation causes Jupiter to have a pronounced equatorial bulge.
Jupiter's atmosphere rotates at different speeds depending on latitude.
This difference is called differential rotation.
The rapid rotation contributes to the formation of strong atmospheric bands.
Jupiter's rotation influences its powerful weather systems.
The rapid spin is important for understanding Jupiter's atmospheric dynamics.

Flares can produce intense electromagnetic radiation.

The solar wind is a continuous flow of charged particles from the Sun.
The solar wind consists mainly of protons and electrons.
The solar wind travels outward through the Solar System.

## 2. BASIC PROPERTIES

Jupiter has a diameter of approximately 139,820 kilometers.
Jupiter has an average distance from the Sun of about 778 million kilometers.
Jupiter receives much less sunlight than Earth because of its greater distance from the Sun.
Jupiter has an average orbital speed of about 13 kilometers per second.
Jupiter's rapid rotation causes a noticeable equatorial bulge.
Jupiter's equatorial diameter is larger than its polar diameter.
Jupiter's density is lower than Earth's because it contains large amounts of hydrogen and helium.
Jupiter's enormous mass produces strong surface-level gravity at its cloud tops.

## SOLAR CELLS

Solar cells convert incoming sunlight into electrical power through the photovoltaic effect.
Spacecraft solar cells are designed for high efficiency and long-term operation.
Solar arrays can be folded during launch and deployed after reaching space.
The available solar power decreases with increasing distance from the Sun.
Radiation can gradually degrade solar-cell performance.
Temperature also affects solar-cell efficiency.
The spacecraft attitude determines how much sunlight reaches the solar arrays.
Sun-tracking or spacecraft pointing strategies can maximize available power.
Solar arrays must be designed to survive launch loads and the space environment.
Power generation is a fundamental constraint for many spacecraft missions.

## 7. MANTLE

The mantle extends from beneath the crust to the outer core.
The mantle makes up most of Earth's volume.
Mantle material is mainly composed of silicate minerals rich in magnesium and iron.
The mantle is mostly solid despite its high temperature.
Heat causes very slow movement within the mantle.
This movement contributes to plate tectonic processes.
The upper mantle contains a region called the asthenosphere.
The asthenosphere can deform more easily than the rigid lithosphere above it.
Heat from Earth's interior can drive mantle convection.
Mantle processes influence volcanism and the movement of tectonic plates.

## HAWKING RADIATION

Hawking radiation is a theoretical prediction combining quantum effects with curved spacetime.
It implies that black holes can emit thermal radiation.
The predicted radiation causes a black hole to gradually lose mass.
The temperature of Hawking radiation decreases as black-hole mass increases.
Astrophysical black holes are expected to have extremely low Hawking temperatures.
Their Hawking radiation is therefore far too weak to be easily detected against ordinary astrophysical backgrounds.
Hawking radiation has not been directly observed from an astrophysical black hole.
If a black hole loses enough mass, its evaporation would accelerate as its temperature rises.
The final stage of black-hole evaporation requires physics beyond the standard semiclassical description.

## ROTATING BLACK HOLES

A rotating black hole is described by the Kerr solution in classical general relativity.
Rotation causes spacetime itself to be dragged around the black hole.
This effect is called frame dragging.
The region where frame dragging becomes unavoidable is called the ergosphere.
The ergosphere lies outside the event horizon of a rotating black hole.
An observer can enter the ergosphere without necessarily crossing the event horizon.
Processes involving the ergosphere can extract rotational energy from a rotating black hole.
The Penrose process is a theoretical mechanism for extracting rotational energy.
Magnetic-field processes can also extract rotational energy and help power relativistic jets.
Black-hole spin can influence the structure of nearby accretion flows.

## **14. Comets**

Comets are small Solar System bodies containing substantial amounts of volatile ices, dust, and rock.

When a comet approaches the Sun, solar heating causes some of its volatile material to transition directly from solid to gas.

This process creates a surrounding coma.

Solar radiation and the solar wind can push material away from the comet, producing tails.

The dust tail and ion tail can point in directions influenced by different physical processes.

Comets are scientifically important because they can preserve primitive material from the early Solar System.

Long-period comets may originate from the distant Oort Cloud.

Short-period comets are often associated with the Kuiper Belt and related populations.

Stars form inside cold, dense regions of interstellar clouds.
These regions contain gas and microscopic dust grains.
Gravity causes sufficiently dense parts of a cloud to collapse.
As a collapsing region contracts, its density and temperature increase.

A protostar is a young stellar object that has not yet begun stable hydrogen fusion.
Material can continue falling onto the protostar from its surrounding disk.

A circumstellar disk can form around the young star.
Planets can eventually form from material remaining in such disks.

citation_map.claim: Cosmology is defined as the scientific study of the universe as a whole, including its origin, evolution, structure, and large-scale properties and behavior [1, 2, 3].
Modern cosmology combines observations with theories from physics and astronomy .
**Key Topics:** Cosmology includes the study of galaxies, cosmic expansion, the cosmic microwave background, dark matter, and dark energy .
It also encompasses the observable universe, which contains stars, gas, dust, radiation, and other forms of matter and energy .
**Age and Size of the Universe:** The universe is approximately 13.8 billion years old according to current measurements .

While the observable universe has a radius larger than 13.8 billion light-years because space has expanded while light was traveling, it is currently unknown whether the entire universe is finite or infinite .
**Key Models and Concepts:** The Big Bang model describes the evolution of the universe from a hot, dense early state [2, 3].
Cosmic expansion refers to the increase of large-scale distances between unbound regions of the universe with time .
Lambda-CDM is the standard cosmological model containing dark energy and cold dark matter .
Other important concepts include redshift, the cosmic microwave background (relic electromagnetic radiation from the early universe), recombination, dark matter, and dark energy .

## COSMOLOGICAL DISTANCES

Cosmology uses several different definitions of distance.
Comoving distance accounts for cosmic expansion when describing large-scale positions.
Proper distance describes physical separation at a specified cosmic time.
Lookback time measures how long light has traveled to reach an observer.
Luminosity distance is defined using the observed brightness of an object.
Angular-diameter distance relates an object's physical size to its observed angular size.

Dark energy is the component associated with the accelerated expansion of the universe.
Lambda-CDM is the standard cosmological model containing dark energy and cold dark matter.
Cosmic web is the large-scale network of galaxies, filaments, clusters, and voids.
Inflation is a proposed period of extremely rapid expansion in the early universe.
Big Bang nucleosynthesis describes the formation of light nuclei during the early universe.
Hubble constant describes the present-day expansion rate of the universe.
Hubble tension refers to disagreement between some independent measurements of the Hubble constant.
Observable universe is the region from which signals have had time to reach Earth.

## 21. Dark Energy

Dark energy is the name given to the component associated with the accelerated expansion of the universe.

Observations of distant supernovae contributed to the discovery that cosmic expansion is accelerating.

Dark energy is one of the major unresolved questions in modern cosmology.

Its physical nature is still unknown.

The simplest cosmological model describes dark energy using a cosmological constant.

More complicated theoretical models have also been proposed.

The show sometimes references dark energy as part of advanced cosmological discussions.

## Lambda-CDM successfully explains many observations across cosmic history.

It describes the formation of large-scale structure from small early density fluctuations.
It reproduces major features of the cosmic microwave background.
It explains the broad evolution of cosmic expansion.
The model contains several measured cosmological parameters.
Some observations, including the Hubble tension and the nature of dark energy, motivate tests beyond the basic model.

## GEOMETRY OF THE UNIVERSE

The geometry of the universe describes its large-scale spatial curvature.
A universe can have positive, zero, or negative spatial curvature.
Positive curvature corresponds to a closed geometry in simple cosmological models.
Zero curvature corresponds to a spatially flat geometry.
Negative curvature corresponds to an open geometry.
CMB observations indicate that the observable universe is very close to spatially flat.
Spatial flatness does not necessarily mean that the entire universe is finite or infinite.
Cosmic geometry depends on the balance of matter, radiation, dark energy, and curvature.
Measurements of the CMB and large-scale structure constrain spatial curvature.
The geometry of spacetime also includes time and is described by general relativity.

## OBSERVATIONAL COSMOLOGY

Observational cosmology uses astronomical measurements to test models of the universe.
The cosmic microwave background is one of its most important datasets.
Type Ia supernovae are used as distance indicators for studying cosmic expansion.
Galaxy surveys measure positions, redshifts, and properties of millions of galaxies.
Baryon acoustic oscillations provide a standard ruler for measuring cosmic distances.
Weak gravitational lensing traces the distribution of matter.
Galaxy clusters provide information about structure growth and dark matter.

Dark energy is the name given to whatever causes the observed accelerated expansion of the universe.
It accounts for a large fraction of the universe's present energy budget in the standard cosmological model.
The simplest model of dark energy is a cosmological constant represented by the symbol Lambda.
In Lambda-CDM, Lambda represents dark energy and CDM represents cold dark matter.
Dark energy differs conceptually from dark matter.
Dark matter increases gravitational attraction and helps structure formation.
Dark energy is associated with the accelerated expansion of space on cosmic scales.
The physical nature of dark energy remains unknown.
Alternative models include evolving forms of dark energy and modified gravity.
## THE BIG BANG

LAMBDA-CDM
Lambda-CDM is the standard model of modern cosmology.
Lambda represents the cosmological constant associated with dark energy.
CDM stands for cold dark matter.
The model also includes ordinary baryonic matter and radiation.

The Big Bang model is supported by several independent observations.
These include cosmic expansion, the cosmic microwave background, and the observed abundance of light elements.
The model describes the evolution of the observable universe but does not by itself explain every question about the ultimate beginning.

Galaxy redshift describes the shift of spectral features toward longer wavelengths.
Cosmological redshift occurs because space expands as light travels through the universe.
For sufficiently distant galaxies, redshift is related to cosmic expansion.
Redshift can be measured from known spectral lines.
Astronomers use redshift to estimate distances and study the history of cosmic expansion.
Higher redshift generally corresponds to observing galaxies at earlier cosmic times.
Very distant galaxies are therefore seen as they existed billions of years ago.
Galaxy surveys use redshift to construct three-dimensional maps of cosmic structure.
Redshift is different from ordinary Doppler shifts caused solely by local motion.

## GEOMETRY OF THE UNIVERSE

The geometry of the universe describes its large-scale spatial curvature.
A universe can have positive, zero, or negative spatial curvature.
Positive curvature corresponds to a closed geometry in simple cosmological models.
Zero curvature corresponds to a spatially flat geometry.
Negative curvature corresponds to an open geometry.
CMB observations indicate that the observable universe is very close to spatially flat.
Spatial flatness does not necessarily mean that the entire universe is finite or infinite.
Cosmic geometry depends on the balance of matter, radiation, dark energy, and curvature.
Measurements of the CMB and large-scale structure constrain spatial curvature.
The geometry of spacetime also includes time and is described by general relativity.

## OBSERVATIONAL COSMOLOGY

Observational cosmology uses astronomical measurements to test models of the universe.
The cosmic microwave background is one of its most important datasets.
Type Ia supernovae are used as distance indicators for studying cosmic expansion.
Galaxy surveys measure positions, redshifts, and properties of millions of galaxies.
Baryon acoustic oscillations provide a standard ruler for measuring cosmic distances.
Weak gravitational lensing traces the distribution of matter.
Galaxy clusters provide information about structure growth and dark matter.

Dark energy is the name given to whatever causes the observed accelerated expansion of the universe.
It accounts for a large fraction of the universe's present energy budget in the standard cosmological model.
The simplest model of dark energy is a cosmological constant represented by the symbol Lambda.
In Lambda-CDM, Lambda represents dark energy and CDM represents cold dark matter.
Dark energy differs conceptually from dark matter.
Dark matter increases gravitational attraction and helps structure formation.
Dark energy is associated with the accelerated expansion of space on cosmic scales.
The physical nature of dark energy remains unknown.
Alternative models include evolving forms of dark energy and modified gravity.
## THE BIG BANG

LAMBDA-CDM
Lambda-CDM is the standard model of modern cosmology.
Lambda represents the cosmological constant associated with dark energy.
CDM stands for cold dark matter.
The model also includes ordinary baryonic matter and radiation.

The Big Bang model is supported by several independent observations.
These include cosmic expansion, the cosmic microwave background, and the observed abundance of light elements.
The model describes the evolution of the observable universe but does not by itself explain every question about the ultimate beginning.

Galaxy redshift describes the shift of spectral features toward longer wavelengths.
Cosmological redshift occurs because space expands as light travels through the universe.
For sufficiently distant galaxies, redshift is related to cosmic expansion.
Redshift can be measured from known spectral lines.
Astronomers use redshift to estimate distances and study the history of cosmic expansion.
Higher redshift generally corresponds to observing galaxies at earlier cosmic times.
Very distant galaxies are therefore seen as they existed billions of years ago.
Galaxy surveys use redshift to construct three-dimensional maps of cosmic structure.
Redshift is different from ordinary Doppler shifts caused solely by local motion.

## 119. Legacy of the Series

The Big Bang Theory remained on television for twelve seasons.

Its long run allowed characters to develop over many years.

The show became closely associated with science-themed sitcom comedy.

Its references to physics, astronomy, engineering, comics, and gaming became recognizable parts of its identity.

Its real-scientist guest appearances further distinguished it from many other sitcoms.

The series remains an important example of science-themed mainstream entertainment.

General relativity describes gravity as the curvature of spacetime caused by mass and energy.
A black hole represents an extreme concentration of gravitational effects.
Near a black hole, spacetime curvature can become extremely strong.
Clocks at different gravitational potentials are measured to run at different rates by distant observers.
This effect is known as gravitational time dilation.
Light escaping a strong gravitational field can experience gravitational redshift.
The closer an emitter is to a black-hole horizon, the greater the gravitational redshift observed from far away.
These effects are consequences of general relativity rather than properties of a physical black-hole surface.
Black holes provide important environments for testing strong-field gravity.

General relativity describes gravity as the curvature of spacetime caused by mass and energy.
A black hole represents an extreme concentration of gravitational effects.
Near a black hole, spacetime curvature can become extremely strong.
Clocks at different gravitational potentials are measured to run at different rates by distant observers.
This effect is known as gravitational time dilation.
Light escaping a strong gravitational field can experience gravitational redshift.
The closer an emitter is to a black-hole horizon, the greater the gravitational redshift observed from far away.
These effects are consequences of general relativity rather than properties of a physical black-hole surface.
Black holes provide important environments for testing strong-field gravity.

The Big Bang Theory remained on television for twelve seasons.

Its long run allowed characters to develop over many years.

The show became closely associated with science-themed sitcom comedy.

Its references to physics, astronomy, engineering, comics, and gaming became recognizable parts of its identity.

Its real-scientist guest appearances further distinguished it from many other sitcoms.

The series remains an important example of science-themed mainstream entertainment.

General relativity describes gravity as the curvature of spacetime caused by mass and energy.
A black hole represents an extreme concentration of gravitational effects.
Near a black hole, spacetime curvature can become extremely strong.
Clocks at different gravitational potentials are measured to run at different rates by distant observers.
This effect is known as gravitational time dilation.
Light escaping a strong gravitational field can experience gravitational redshift.
The closer an emitter is to a black-hole horizon, the greater the gravitational redshift observed from far away.
These effects are consequences of general relativity rather than properties of a physical black-hole surface.
Black holes provide important environments for testing strong-field gravity.

General relativity describes gravity as the curvature of spacetime caused by mass and energy.
A black hole represents an extreme concentration of gravitational effects.
Near a black hole, spacetime curvature can become extremely strong.
Clocks at different gravitational potentials are measured to run at different rates by distant observers.
This effect is known as gravitational time dilation.
Light escaping a strong gravitational field can experience gravitational redshift.
The closer an emitter is to a black-hole horizon, the greater the gravitational redshift observed from far away.
These effects are consequences of general relativity rather than properties of a physical black-hole surface.
Black holes provide important environments for testing strong-field gravity.

## OBSERVATIONAL COSMOLOGY

Observational cosmology uses astronomical measurements to test models of the universe.
The cosmic microwave background is one of its most important datasets.
Type Ia supernovae are used as distance indicators for studying cosmic expansion.
Galaxy surveys measure positions, redshifts, and properties of millions of galaxies.
Baryon acoustic oscillations provide a standard ruler for measuring cosmic distances.
Weak gravitational lensing traces the distribution of matter.
Galaxy clusters provide information about structure growth and dark matter.

The Big Bang model is supported by several independent observations.
These include cosmic expansion, the cosmic microwave background, and the observed abundance of light elements.
The model describes the evolution of the observable universe but does not by itself explain every question about the ultimate beginning.

## 31. George Smoot

George Smoot is an American astrophysicist and cosmologist.

He received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 2006 with John Mather.

Their work involved measurements of the cosmic microwave background using the COBE satellite.

The cosmic microwave background is electromagnetic radiation originating from the early universe.

Smoot appeared on The Big Bang Theory as himself.

His presence connects the fictional characters to real observational cosmology.

His scientific background is particularly relevant to the show's references to the early universe and cosmology.

## 20. Dark Matter

Dark matter is a term used for matter inferred from gravitational effects that does not appear to interact strongly with electromagnetic radiation.

Astronomers have observed gravitational phenomena that cannot be fully explained by visible matter alone.

Examples include galaxy rotation and gravitational lensing.

Dark matter remains an active area of scientific research.

The exact identity of dark matter is not yet established.

The concept is frequently mentioned in discussions of cosmology and astrophysics.

Raj's scientific interests make astronomy and cosmology natural subjects for the series.

Lithium observations show some unresolved differences with simple theoretical predictions.
Big Bang nucleosynthesis is one of the major tests of early-universe cosmology.
It connects nuclear physics with the history of cosmic expansion.

LAMBDA-CDM
Lambda-CDM is the standard model of modern cosmology.
Lambda represents the cosmological constant associated with dark energy.
CDM stands for cold dark matter.
The model also includes ordinary baryonic matter and radiation.

The entire universe may be much larger than the observable universe.

## 13. INTERIOR

Venus is expected to have a metallic core.
A rocky mantle surrounds the core.
A rocky crust forms the outer solid layer.
The interior structure is broadly similar to that of Earth.
The exact physical state of Venus's core is not completely known.
Scientists use gravity measurements and geological observations to study Venus's interior.
The planet's interior heat influences its geological activity.
Understanding the interior helps explain volcanism and tectonic deformation.

## 14. RING MOONS

Several moons orbit within or near Saturn's ring system.
Some small moons are called shepherd moons.
Shepherd moons can confine or shape narrow ring structures.
Prometheus and Pandora interact strongly with Saturn's F ring.
Pan and Daphnis occupy regions associated with gaps in the rings.
Moon-ring interactions create waves and disturbances.
The gravitational influence of moons helps maintain some ring features.
The rings and moons form an interconnected dynamical system.
Studying these interactions helps explain how planetary ring systems evolve.

## 54. Raj and Astronomy

Raj's professional identity is strongly connected with astronomy.

Astronomy studies celestial objects and phenomena.

Astrophysics applies physics to understand astronomical systems.

Raj's conversations frequently involve planets, stars, galaxies, and cosmology.

His career demonstrates the relationship between observational astronomy and theoretical physics.

The series uses Raj's astronomy expertise to introduce scientific ideas that differ from Sheldon's theoretical work.

## 94. General Relativity

General relativity is Albert Einstein's theory of gravitation.

It describes gravity in terms of the geometry of spacetime.

Mass and energy influence spacetime curvature.

Objects move through this curved spacetime according to the theory's equations.

General relativity predicts phenomena such as gravitational time dilation, gravitational lensing, and black holes.

The theory is frequently relevant to discussions of cosmology and astrophysics.

## COSMOLOGICAL DISTANCES

Cosmology uses several different definitions of distance.
Comoving distance accounts for cosmic expansion when describing large-scale positions.
Proper distance describes physical separation at a specified cosmic time.
Lookback time measures how long light has traveled to reach an observer.
Luminosity distance is defined using the observed brightness of an object.
Angular-diameter distance relates an object's physical size to its observed angular size.

## 97. Cosmological Expansion

The universe is expanding on large scales.

Galaxies generally show increasing recession velocities with increasing distance.

This relationship is described by Hubble's law in appropriate contexts.

Modern cosmology uses more precise models involving the expansion history of the universe.

The Big Bang model describes the universe evolving from an early hot, dense state.

The show occasionally references these cosmological ideas through Raj and Sheldon.

## 117. Stephen Hawking and Scientific Popular Culture

Stephen Hawking became an important figure in public discussions of cosmology and black holes.

His books introduced difficult scientific ideas to broad audiences.

His appearance on The Big Bang Theory reflects his cultural importance.

The show treats him as both a respected scientist and a participant in comedy.

His presence is an example of how real scientists can become cultural figures beyond academia.

## 18. Cosmology

Cosmology is the scientific study of the universe as a whole.

It includes questions about the universe's origin, structure, evolution, and large-scale behavior.

Raj's astrophysics background frequently connects him to cosmological topics.

Cosmology includes the study of galaxies, cosmic expansion, the cosmic microwave background, dark matter, and dark energy.

The Big Bang model is the leading scientific framework describing the early hot, dense state of the observable universe.

The television series itself is not primarily about cosmology despite its title.

The title uses the scientific phrase "Big Bang Theory" as the name of a comedy centered on scientists.

COSMOLOGY
Cosmology is the scientific study of the origin, evolution, structure, and large-scale properties of the universe.
Modern cosmology combines observations with theories from physics and astronomy.
The observable universe contains galaxies, stars, gas, dust, dark matter, radiation, and other forms of matter and energy.
The universe is approximately 13.8 billion years old according to current measurements.
The observable universe is larger than 13.8 billion light-years in radius because space has expanded while light was traveling.
The observable universe is the region from which light or other signals have had time to reach us.
The entire universe may be much larger than the observable universe.
Whether the entire universe is finite or infinite is not currently known.

The entire universe may be much larger than the observable universe.
Whether the entire universe is finite or infinite is not currently known.
Cosmology studies the universe on scales much larger than individual galaxies.
The standard cosmological model is commonly called Lambda-CDM.

## OBSERVATIONAL COSMOLOGY

Observational cosmology uses astronomical measurements to test models of the universe.
The cosmic microwave background is one of its most important datasets.
Type Ia supernovae are used as distance indicators for studying cosmic expansion.
Galaxy surveys measure positions, redshifts, and properties of millions of galaxies.
Baryon acoustic oscillations provide a standard ruler for measuring cosmic distances.
Weak gravitational lensing traces the distribution of matter.
Galaxy clusters provide information about structure growth and dark matter.

## 97. Cosmological Expansion

The universe is expanding on large scales.

Galaxies generally show increasing recession velocities with increasing distance.

This relationship is described by Hubble's law in appropriate contexts.

Modern cosmology uses more precise models involving the expansion history of the universe.

The Big Bang model describes the universe evolving from an early hot, dense state.

The show occasionally references these cosmological ideas through Raj and Sheldon.

## COSMOLOGICAL DISTANCES

Cosmology uses several different definitions of distance.
Comoving distance accounts for cosmic expansion when describing large-scale positions.
Proper distance describes physical separation at a specified cosmic time.
Lookback time measures how long light has traveled to reach an observer.
Luminosity distance is defined using the observed brightness of an object.
Angular-diameter distance relates an object's physical size to its observed angular size.

LAMBDA-CDM
Lambda-CDM is the standard model of modern cosmology.
Lambda represents the cosmological constant associated with dark energy.
CDM stands for cold dark matter.
The model also includes ordinary baryonic matter and radiation.

Conditions required for generating a matter-antimatter asymmetry are studied in particle physics and cosmology.
The observed asymmetry is an important unresolved problem in fundamental physics.
Understanding baryogenesis could explain why ordinary matter exists in large quantities today.

Cosmology means the scientific study of the universe as a whole.
Big Bang model describes the evolution of the universe from a hot, dense early state.
Cosmic expansion means that large-scale distances between unbound regions of the universe increase with time.
Redshift is the shift of observed spectral features toward longer wavelengths.
Cosmic microwave background is relic electromagnetic radiation from the early universe.
Recombination is the epoch when electrons combined with nuclei to form neutral atoms.
Dark matter is matter inferred primarily from gravitational effects.
Dark energy is the component associated with the accelerated expansion of the universe.
Lambda-CDM is the standard cosmological model containing dark energy and cold dark matter.

INFLATION
Inflation is a proposed period of extremely rapid expansion in the very early universe.
Inflation can explain why widely separated regions of the observable universe have similar large-scale properties.
It can also explain why the observable universe appears close to spatially flat.
Quantum fluctuations during inflation can become seeds for later cosmic structure.
These fluctuations can be stretched to enormous scales during rapid expansion.
Inflation is supported indirectly by several features of observed cosmological structure.
The specific physical mechanism responsible for inflation has not been established.
Different inflationary models propose different fields and potential energy landscapes.
